notes: This sheet is drawn in a very light dashed pencil: almost every wire is a broken chain of 3-15 px strokes, so 'gap' by itself never means 'no connection' here. Every net below was traced at 10-20x and the reading is the one in which each dash chain is collinear with the next. All five triangles point UP (apex = output at the top, both inputs on the bottom edge). Op-Amp 23 carries explicit pin marks - '-' on the LEFT, '+' on the RIGHT (read at 14x) - and Op-Amp 8 shows a '+' beside its right lead, so throughout this sheet LEFT bottom lead = in- (index 1), RIGHT bottom lead = in+ (index 0), apex = out (index 2). That reading is corroborated everywhere: on Op-Amps 3, 8, 21 and 23 the right lead runs straight to a GND symbol while the left lead carries the feedback element. Net map (12 nets). 0 = the single ground reference; all six GND symbols share it - GND 19 (Op-Amp 3 in+), GND 11 (Op-Amp 8 in+), GND 16 (Op-Amp 21 in+), GND 15 (Op-Amp 23 in+), GND 18 (V-DC 0 right terminal), GND 12 (I-DC 10 right terminal). n1 = the top rail at y~39-49: Resistor 2 top (x=117), Resistor 7 top (x=327), Resistor 6 top (x=457). Judgment calls: (a) The top rail has a genuinely blank ~42 px gap between x=329 (Resistor 7's top lead) and x=371 (checked at 20x - no faint ink at all), larger than the sheet's usual 10-25 px dash gaps. I still read it as ONE rail, because the two segments are collinear (y=46 vs y=47), the right segment's left end at (371,47) is a bare free end with no corner, and splitting the rail would leave Resistor 6's top terminal as a one-terminal net - a Tier-1 fault - while the joined reading reproduces the three-resistor floating star that this drafter uses in the sibling sheets. (b) Similar sub-15 px dash gaps were read as continuous at: Resistor 2 bottom (112,124) to the Op-Amp 1 output corner (111,137); Op-Amp 1's left lead end (97,209) to the Inductor 9 / Resistor 4 corner (94,213); Op-Amp 3's left lead end (65,406) to the Capacitor 20 / V-DC corner (64,419); Op-Amp 8's left lead end (328,427) to the I-DC riser at (326,441); Op-Amp 23's left lead end (441,217) to the Inductor 22 / Capacitor 14 corner (439,225). In each case the fragments are collinear to within 3 px and the alternative would strand a source or leave an op-amp input open. (c) The mid rail (y~279-290) and the top rail (y~39-49) cross no other wire - every vertical they meet terminates on them - so there are no hop-vs-junction decisions anywhere in this drawing. (d) 2-terminal parts are listed top-then-bottom as drawn; V-DC 0 and I-DC 10 are listed left-then-right, their right terminals being the ones facing GND 18 and GND 12. This does not affect any metric. (e) Tier-2 note: n1 has no DC path to ground except through the three op-amp outputs, and n5 sits between a voltage source and a capacitor. Both are what the ink shows and are left as drawn. No component was added, removed or re-classed.
